title: Cloning-Free Targeting of Endogenous Loci to Generate Fluorescent Reporters in Medaka
author: Simon Knoblich
license_note: PMC full-text XML — Bio-protocol — CC-BY confirmed in article XML

steps.title: Prepare 100× ERM stock
steps.instruction: Weigh 100 g NaCl, 3 g KCl, 3.02 g CaCl₂·2H₂O, and 7.81 g MgSO₄·7H₂O, fill to 1 L with dH₂O, autoclave, and store at room temperature.

steps.title: Make 1× ERM working solution
steps.instruction: Combine 17 mL 100× ERM, 10 mL 1 M HEPES pH 7.5 (NaOH‑adjusted), 2 mL 5 M NaCl, fill to 1 L with dH₂O, autoclave, and store at room temperature.

steps.title: Prepare fin‑clip buffer
steps.instruction: Dissolve 48.45 g TRIS‑HCl (400 mM) in 100 mL water, add 1.46 g EDTA (5 mM) in 5 mL, add 8.76 g NaCl (150 mM) in 15 mL, add 1 g SDS (0.1 % w/v) in 2.5 mL, fill to 500 mL with dH₂O, filter‑sterilize, store at room temperature; add 50 µL Proteinase K (20 mg/mL) to 1 mL buffer fresh before use.

steps.title: Prepare 0.4% Tricaine solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 400 mg Tricaine powder in 2.1 mL 1 M TRIS‑HCl pH 9.0, bring volume to 100 mL with dH₂O, adjust pH to 7.0, autoclave, and store at –20 °C in the dark.

steps.title: Linearize Cas9 plasmid
steps.instruction: Set up a 50 µL digestion with ~10 µg pCS2‑Cas9 plasmid, 5 µL CutSmart 10× buffer, 1.5 µL NotI‑HF, and nuclease‑free dH₂O to volume; incubate at 37 °C for 3 h.

steps.title: Purify linearized plasmid
steps.instruction: Purify the digested plasmid using a QIAquick PCR Purification kit, measure concentration on a Nanodrop, and dilute the eluate to ≈100 ng/µL with nuclease‑free H₂O.

steps.title: In‑vitro transcribe Cas9 mRNA
steps.instruction: Mix 6 µL linearized template (≈100 ng/µL), 10 µL 2× NTP/Cap buffer, 2 µL 10× transcription buffer, 2 µL SP6 enzyme; incubate 37 °C for 2 h, add 1 µL TurboDNAse, incubate 37 °C 15 min.

steps.title: Purify and aliquot Cas9 mRNA
steps.instruction: Purify the transcription product with a RNeasy Mini kit, elute in 35 µL nuclease‑free H₂O, measure concentration, aliquot to obtain 150 ng/µL in a 10 µL injection mix (e.g., 3 µL if stock is 500 ng/µL), and store aliquots at –80 °C.

steps.title: Aliquot recombinant Cas9 protein
steps.instruction: Make 1 µL single‑use aliquots of IDT glycerol‑free Cas9 (10 µg/µL, 61 µM) in PCR strips, store at –20 °C and avoid freeze‑thaw cycles.

steps.title: Design guide RNA target
steps.instruction: Locate the gene in the Ensembl medaka HdrR genome, select the desired transcript, download its genomic sequence, choose an insertion site, identify a 20‑nt protospacer upstream of an NGG PAM, ensure GC 50‑70 % and no 3′ C, and verify minimal distance between cut site and insertion.

steps.title: Order and prepare synthetic sgRNA
steps.instruction: Order the 20‑nt sgRNA from Sigma, upon receipt spin down, add 30 µL nuclease‑free H₂O to obtain 3 nmol (100 µM, 3.2 µg/µL), mix gently, store at –80 °C; for mRNA injections make a 10 µM working dilution in nuclease‑free H₂O and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Design repair‑donor primers
steps.instruction: Create forward and reverse primers with 5′ biotin, containing 32‑40 bp homology arms, optional recoded spanning sequence, and 19‑21 nt annealing region to the fluorescent reporter; order salt‑free primers at 100 µM and store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Assemble PCR for donor synthesis
steps.instruction: For each 50 µL reaction add 0.1 µL fluorescent reporter plasmid (~100 ng/µL), 0.25 µL forward primer (100 µM), 0.25 µL reverse primer (100 µM), 25 µL 2× Phusion or Q5 master mix, and 24.4 µL nuclease‑free H₂O. Prepare a master mix for 4‑8 reactions if higher yield is needed.

steps.title: Run donor PCR
steps.instruction: Thermal cycle: 98 °C 2 min; 30 cycles of 98 °C 30 s, 61.5 °C 30 s, 72 °C 45 s; final extension 72 °C 10 min; hold at 10 °C.

steps.title: Optimize PCR if needed
steps.instruction: If nonspecific bands appear, perform a gradient PCR (60‑72 °C annealing) or add 3 % v/v DMSO (1.5 µL per 50 µL reaction).

steps.title: Verify and purify donor PCR product
steps.instruction: Run an agarose gel with Orange‑G loading dye, confirm a single band (~900 bp), then purify using a MinElute PCR Purification kit (pool up to eight 50 µL reactions per column), elute in 10 µL nuclease‑free H₂O, measure concentration (~100 ng/µL), and store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Optional gel‑purify long primers donor
steps.instruction: If any primer exceeds 65 nt or ultrapure donor is required, gel‑purify the PCR product with a MinElute Gel Extraction kit, then perform a second MinElute PCR purification.

steps.title: Siliconize injection capillaries
steps.instruction: Under a fume hood, load 20 µL Sigmacote into a borosilicate capillary using a shortened gel‑loading tip, swirl to coat the interior, remove excess liquid, let reagent evaporate overnight at room temperature, flush with nuclease‑free H₂O, remove water, let dry, then pull microinjection needles.

steps.title: Prepare injection mix with Cas9 mRNA
steps.instruction: In a tube combine 0.5 µL sgRNA (10 µM, 0.32 µg/µL) → final 0.5 µM, 1.5 µg Cas9 mRNA (final 150 ng/µL), 100 ng linear PCR donor (final 10 ng/µL), add nuclease‑free H₂O to 10 µL total, centrifuge 6,000 × g 5 s, keep on ice and use the same day.

steps.title: Prepare injection mix with Cas9 protein
steps.instruction: Thaw reagents to room temperature, then add in order: 1 µL recombinant Cas9 (10 µg/µL) → final 1 µg/µL, 1.22 µL sgRNA (100 µM) → final 12.2 µM, 400 ng linear donor → final 40 ng/µL, nuclease‑free H₂O to 10 µL total; centrifuge 6,000 × g 5 s, keep at room temperature and use within 1–2 h.

steps.title: Inject 1‑cell embryos
steps.instruction: Load the appropriate mix into siliconized capillaries, pull needles, calibrate to deliver ~10‑15 % of cell volume, inject 1‑cell stage medaka embryos, then transfer up to 50 embryos per 10 cm dish containing 1× ERM.

steps.title: Incubate injected embryos
steps.instruction: Incubate embryos at 27 °C, change 1× ERM daily, remove dead embryos, and monitor until hatching.

steps.title: Screen embryos for fluorescence
steps.instruction: Examine embryos daily (or at expected expression stage) under a fluorescence stereoscope; select the brightest, ubiquitously expressing individuals and raise them separately as potential founders (F0).

steps.title: Prepare fin‑clip buffer for DNA extraction
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL Proteinase K (20 mg/mL) to 1 mL fin‑clip buffer, aliquot 50 µL per labeled 1.5 mL tube, keep on ice.

steps.title: Fin‑clip and lyse tissue
steps.instruction: Anesthetize fish in 0.4 % Tricaine, cut a small caudal fin piece, place it in a tube with 50 µL prepared buffer, rinse instruments with 70 % EtOH and dH₂O between fish, spin briefly, incubate 65 °C ≥4 h, add 100 µL dH₂O, mix, heat 95 °C 15 min to inactivate Proteinase K, spin 1 min, keep 2 µL supernatant as gDNA template.

steps.title: Set up genotyping PCR
steps.instruction: Combine 2 µL fin‑clip gDNA, 0.25 µL forward primer (100 µM), 0.25 µL reverse primer (100 µM), 25 µL 2× Phusion or Q5 Master Mix, and 22.5 µL nuclease‑free H₂O (total 50 µL).

steps.title: Run genotyping PCR
steps.instruction: Thermal cycle: 98 °C 2 min; 30 cycles of 98 °C 30 s, annealing 30 s at the primer‑determined optimal temperature (60‑72 °C), 72 °C 45 s; final extension 72 °C 10 min; hold at 10 °C.

steps.title: Analyze PCR products
steps.instruction: Run reactions on an agarose gel with an appropriate DNA ladder, visualize bands (≈500 bp wild‑type, ≈1,200 bp insertion); gel‑purify insertion band for Sanger sequencing or purify PCR directly for sequencing with internal primers.

steps.title: Outcross F0 founders
steps.instruction: When F0 fish reach sexual maturity, cross each individually with wild‑type fish, collect ≥100 F1 embryos per cross, and screen daily for fluorescence as described above.

steps.title: Raise and genotype F1 candidates
steps.instruction: Raise 20‑40 fluorescent F1 embryos to adulthood, fin‑clip each, extract gDNA as before, perform genotyping PCR, and sequence to confirm correct KI allele.

steps.title: Establish stable KI line
steps.instruction: Use confirmed F1 carriers for further outcrosses to maintain the line; optionally intercross to obtain homozygous individuals and assess phenotypes. Do not discard F1s with minor scarred integrations, as they may still produce functional fusions.
